title: A provider timestamp in the future is never stale (ageMinutes clamps to 0); 6,661 of 19,194 snapshots have ts after pulled_at
steps: odds_snapshots: ts > pulled_at for 6661 rows; in the 2026-11-18 replay ts is exactly +3.0 h vs pulled_at (1260 rows)
edges_log rows from first_shown_at 2026-11-18T00:08:22Z (6 rows): price_ts is 03:07-03:08Z, 3 h after the edge was "first shown" and ~2 h after game start (Atlanta Hawks +3.5 fanduel, start 01:11Z)
packages/core/src/feed.ts ageMinutes: Math.max(0, (now - t)/60000), so a future last_update is age 0, fresh
expected: price_ts (book last_update) can never be later than the fetch/log time; such a value should be untrusted, not fresh. A logged edge needs price_ts <= first_shown_at <= start_time.
actual: Clock skew or a bad provider timestamp passes the stale check. Part of this is a demo-replay artifact, but it is what the Results page shows for the first 6 logged edges and no code guards it.
evidence: edges_log id 53ea8d1e-d2bf-45a4-8b83-7db8f8aab85c (price_ts 2026-11-18T03:08:18Z, first_shown 00:08:22Z, start 01:11:22Z) and 5 more. The 5 edges logged 2026-11-21 are consistent.
